newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh flood toll reaches 36, may rise.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh flood toll reaches 36, may rise.

text.p: Floods sweeping large parts of Bangladesh have killed at least 36 people and made a quarter of a million others homeless, officials said on Saturday.

They said at least half a million people were marooned in their half-submerged homes as the floods gripped 19 out of the country's 64 administrative districts. Worst hit were 10 districts in the southeast, including Chittagong, Cox's Bazar and the Chittagong Hill Tracts, where all the deaths occurred.

The victims died in landslides, house collapses and by drowning. At least 100 people were injured, local officials and police said on Saturday. Unofficial sources on Saturday put the death toll at more than 50. A mild tremor also jolted Chittagong port city and nearby areas on Friday night, but its strength and epicentre were not known because the country's only seismological observatory was closed.
"We felt the rockings twice while the city was being pounded by torrential rain. They lasted for five or ten seconds and there was no report of damage," one Chittagong official said.
Weather officials said the floods could spread further and death counts could go up with more rains expected in next few days.

Heavy showers on Saturday disrupted life in the Bangladesh capital Dhaka, a city of nine million people, many of whom live in slums. Low areas on the city's outskirts have been inundated, witnesses said.
More than 50,000 people have been shifted to flood shelters and many more moved to higher ground on their own, officials said.
Road links between Chittagong and neighbouring districts, including Cox's Bazar, have become impassable as floodwater washed away several small bridges and partly inundated highways.
Train communications at different sections of the affected areas were disrupted because tracks were flooded or under threat, said Farhad Reja, General Manager of Bangladesh's eastern railway.
Handling of cargo at the Chittagong port was hampered, port officials said. The national airline Bangladesh Biman said flights to and from Chittagong were delayed or suspended.

Movement of ships at Chittagong port became risky because of strong currents and waves at the Karnaphuli river linking the port to the Bay of Bengal, port officials said. Work at the country's second sea port at Mongla, in Khulna district, was also partially disrupted, port operators told reporters on Saturday. Floodwaters have inundated at least 50 villages in the northeastern tea-growing district of Sylhet, local officials told reporters.
They said road links between Sylhet and neighboiuring districts had been threatened by fast rising rivers and water rushing in from Indian hills across the broder.

Poor visibility caused by heavy rain forced a Chittagong-bound Singaporean helicopter, chartered by Nepalese private airline Manakanan Airways, to land at a playground at Kumira, 25 km (15 miles) north of Chittagong on Friday evening, police said.

Official BSS news agency earlier said the helicopter was flying from Calcutta to Rangoon via Chittagong. At least 300,000 acres (120,000 hectares) of crop-land have been inundated, agriculture officials said on Thursday, but they could not immediately provide loss estimates.
The weekend in Bangladesh falls on Friday and Saturday.
